fineness.label: What is fineness?
fineness.text: Fineness is the share of pure metal in the alloy, in parts per thousand: 585 gold is 58.5% pure gold. It should match the hallmark on the item.

carat.label: What is a carat?
carat.text: A carat (ct) is the weight of a gemstone: 1 carat is 0.2 grams. Not to be confused with the karat of gold, which is another way to state fineness.

color.label: What is diamond colour?
color.text: Colour is graded by letter from D (colourless) to Z (light yellow or brown tint). D-F count as colourless, G-J as near colourless.

clarity.label: What is clarity?
clarity.text: Clarity shows how visible a stone's internal and surface flaws are: FL and IF (flawless), VVS1-VVS2, VS1-VS2, SI1-SI2, I1-I3. It is graded under 10x magnification.

About.title: What is Jeparla?
About.lead: Jeparla is an online catalog that brings together gold, silver and diamond jewelry stores in Azerbaijan.
About.how: You search products by store, category, metal, fineness, weight and price, then message the store directly on WhatsApp about the piece you like. Jeparla itself does not sell products or take payments.

what.a: A catalog that shows products from jewelry stores in Azerbaijan on one site: gold, silver and diamond jewelry.

buy.q: How do I buy on Jeparla?
buy.a: Press the WhatsApp button on a product page: the message includes the product name, code and link. Purchase, payment and delivery are agreed directly with the store.

price.a: A seller can set a fixed price or a metal-linked one. Metal-linked prices update automatically with the daily metal rates of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan, and the update date is shown next to the product.

verified.q: What does the Verified badge mean?
verified.a: Seller and document checks are done separately and each is shown on its own. A check that was not done is shown as not performed.

sell.q: How do I add my store to Jeparla?
sell.a: Apply through Open a store. After the store is checked, its products go through moderation and then appear in the catalog.

Help.title: Help and support
Help.description: How to contact a store, list your catalog, upload documents, what verification means and how to report a problem.
Help.intro: Short answers for buyers and sellers.

contact.q: How do I contact a store?
contact.a: Press the WhatsApp button on a product page: the message already includes the product name, code and link. Price, payment and delivery are agreed directly with the store. Jeparla itself does not sell products or take payments.

sell.q: How do I list my store's catalog?
sell.a: Apply through Open a store: account, store details, documents and an optional first product. After the store is checked you add products from your dashboard; each product is reviewed before it appears in the catalog.

documents.a: Upload them as PDF, JPG or PNG in the Documents step of the sign-up, or later from your dashboard. Documents are kept in private storage and only the checking team looks at them. Gold, silver and diamond sellers go through a document check; bijouterie sellers are not asked for certificates.

verified.a: Seller and document checks are done separately and each is shown on its own on the store and product pages. A check that was not done is shown as not performed. A check confirms the documents we were shown; it is not a guarantee for a particular piece, so confirm the product with the store before you buy.

report.q: How do I report a problem?
report.a: If a product's details are wrong or the product looks suspicious, use the Report button on the product page. For anything else, see Support below.

support.title: Support
support.text: If you have a question or a problem, write to us:
support.none: A direct support address has not been published yet; it will be shown on this page once it is. Sellers can correct the details of a returned product or store in the dashboard and send it for review again.

SizeGuide.title: Size guide: rings, bracelets and chains
SizeGuide.metaTitle: Ring size chart, bracelet and chain lengths
SizeGuide.description: How to find your ring size at home: inner diameter and circumference in mm, the ISO 8653 size, a size helper, and bracelet and chain lengths.
SizeGuide.answer: In Azerbaijan a ring size is the ring's inner diameter in millimetres: a size 17 ring is 17 mm across inside. Sizes usually go in steps of 0.5. Measure around your finger and enter it in the helper below to see the nearest size.

honest.title: Measuring at home is approximate
honest.text: A measurement taken at home can be off by half a size to a full size. Confirm the size with the store before you order: many stores measure in person, and some can resize a ring.
honest.noPrintable: We do not offer a printable ring sizer: printers and PDF viewers often shrink or enlarge the page, so a printed ruler can be off by several millimetres. That is more than the step between two sizes (0.5 mm of diameter).

rings.title: Ring size chart
rings.intro: The size number equals the inner diameter. The circumference is the diameter times π, rounded to one decimal.
rings.caption: Ring sizes: Azerbaijan size, inner diameter, inner circumference and ISO 8653 size
rings.sourceAz: Azerbaijan and CIS size: the inner diameter in millimetres, in steps of 0.5. This is the convention stores use; we did not find the text of a current standard we could cite.
rings.sourceIso: ISO 8653:2016 (Jewellery — Ring-sizes — Definition, measurement and designation) designates a ring size by its inner circumference in mm; most of Europe uses this system. In the chart the ISO size is the circumference rounded to a whole millimetre.
rings.sourceUs: US sizes are not shown: we found no current published standard for that conversion, and we will not invent one.
rings.rounding: Every number comes from exact decimal arithmetic, with halves rounded up.

helper.title: Ring size helper
helper.intro: Enter the number you measured. Measure around the finger with a thread or a paper strip, or measure across an existing ring.
helper.hint: For example 53.5. A dot or a comma, at most two decimals.
helper.empty: The nearest size appears here once you enter a number.
helper.invalid: Enter a number in millimetres, for example 53.5.
helper.outOfRange: This is outside the chart (sizes 15 to 24). Check that you chose the right measurement, or ask the store.
helper.details: Inner diameter {diameter} mm, inner circumference {circumference} mm, ISO 8653 size {iso}.
helper.tie: Exactly half-way between two sizes, the helper picks the larger one.
helper.confirm: This is an estimate. Confirm with the store before you order.

measure.title: How to find your ring size at home
measure.ringTitle: With a ring you already have

ringSteps.s1: Pick a thin, round ring that fits the same finger comfortably.
ringSteps.s2: Lay it on a ruler marked in millimetres.
ringSteps.s3: Measure across the widest part, from inside edge to inside edge, without the metal.
ringSteps.s4: That number in millimetres is your size. In the helper, choose "Inside diameter of a ring".

measure.stringTitle: With a thread or a paper strip

stringSteps.s1: Take a thread that does not stretch, or a paper strip about 5 mm wide.
stringSteps.s2: Wrap it around the base of the finger, snug but not tight.
stringSteps.s3: Mark where the ends meet with a pen.
stringSteps.s4: Unwrap it and measure up to the mark with a ruler, in millimetres: that is the circumference.
stringSteps.s5: Enter the number in the helper and check that the ring will pass over the knuckle.

tips.t1: Measure at the end of the day in a warm room: fingers are thinner in the cold and fuller in the heat.
tips.t2: Measure two or three times and compare.
tips.t3: If the knuckle is wider than the base of the finger, the ring has to pass over it: measure both.
tips.t4: A wide band (about 6 mm or more) sits tighter; ask the store whether you need half a size up.

diagram.title: Inner diameter and inner circumference of a ring
diagram.desc: The straight line across the inside of the ring is the inner diameter; the circle along the inside edge is the inner circumference.

bracelets.title: Bracelet length
bracelets.intro: Measure the wrist just above the wrist bone with a thread or a strip. For a chain bracelet to sit comfortably, 1 to 2 cm is usually added to the wrist measurement.
bracelets.caption: Bracelet lengths and who they usually fit

r2.use: A frequent length for women's bracelets

r3.use: A looser women's fit or a smaller men's bracelet

r4.use: A frequent length for men's bracelets

bracelets.bangle: A rigid bangle that does not open has to pass over the hand: touch the thumb to the little finger, measure around the widest part of the hand, and ask the store for the bangle's inner size.
bracelets.note: These lengths are general guidance, not a standard; stores and designs differ.

chains.title: Chain length
chains.intro: A chain is measured laid flat, clasp included. Where it sits depends on the neck and on any pendant.
chains.caption: Chain lengths and where they usually sit

r1.use: Close to the base of the neck

r2.use: At the collarbone; a frequent choice for a pendant

r4.use: At the neckline; frequent for men's chains

r6.use: A long chain over clothing; can be worn doubled

chains.note: The simplest way: lay a chain you already own flat, measure it, and choose shorter or longer from how you like it.

sources.trade: Azerbaijan and CIS size numbers (inner diameter, mm): the convention used by stores.
sources.lengths: Bracelet and chain lengths: general guidance, not a standard.

SellLanding.title: Put your jewellery store where buyers are searching
SellLanding.lead: Jeparla brings Azerbaijan's jewellery stores together in one catalogue. Buyers search by fineness, weight and price, then message you directly on WhatsApp. Listing in the catalogue is free.

catalog.title: A free catalogue and your own link
catalog.text: All your products on one page, with fineness, weight, size and stones. Put your store link in your Instagram bio or in a message.

price.title: Prices update themselves every day
price.text: Mark a product as "metal-linked" and its price follows the Central Bank of Azerbaijan's daily rate. No more editing the price list by hand every morning.

verified.title: Jeparla Verified badge
verified.text: Once your documents are checked, a badge appears on your store and products. Buyers see who was checked and what was checked.

search.title: Buyers from search
search.text: Buyers search for things like "585 gold ring" and filter. Your products are found by category, metal and price.

whatsapp.title: Straight to WhatsApp
whatsapp.text: No middleman: the buyer writes to you with the product name, code and link. The sale and payment are between you and the buyer.

1.title: Account and store

2.title: Documents
2.text: Upload your tax ID (VÖEN) and store documents; the team checks them. The result appears in your dashboard.

3.title: Products
3.text: Add photos, fineness, weight and price. A product appears in the catalogue after review.

fee.q: How much does it cost to be on Jeparla?
fee.a: Listing your store and products in the catalogue is free. Commission terms are still being decided; if any apply, they will be agreed in advance in a written agreement, and nothing is charged without your consent.

documents.a: Your tax ID (VÖEN), the store registration certificate or the hallmark stamp document (PDF, JPG or PNG). Documents are used only for the check and are never shown publicly.

time.a: The registration form takes a few minutes. Document checks depend on the team's queue; you see the result in your dashboard.

prices.q: Can I set my own prices?
prices.a: Yes. For each product you choose a fixed price or a "metal-linked" price. A metal-linked price is calculated from the Central Bank rate, the weight and your making charge.

sales.a: No. Jeparla does not take orders or payments. The buyer writes to you on WhatsApp; the deal and payment are between you and the buyer.

guide.background: Use a plain, light, single-colour background (white paper, cream cloth).

Calculator.title: Gold and silver calculator
Calculator.description: Today's metal value of gold and silver by weight and fineness, in manat, at the daily rate of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan.
Calculator.intro: Enter the weight and fineness of a piece to see what its metal is worth today at the rate of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan (CBAR).
Calculator.weightHint: For example 4.2 or 4,2; at most 3 decimals.
Calculator.prompt: Enter the weight to see the metal value.
Calculator.purePrice: CBAR price ({metal}, pure metal): {gram} per gram, {ounce} per troy ounce
Calculator.weekendNote: On weekends and holidays the last rate CBAR published is used.
Calculator.notShopPrice: This is the value of the metal only, not a shop price: workmanship, stones and the store's margin are extra.

errors.format: Enter the weight as a number, for example 4.2.
errors.notPositive: The weight must be greater than zero.
errors.tooPrecise: Use at most 3 decimals (down to a milligram).
errors.tooLarge: The weight cannot be more than 10,000 grams.

Calculator.unavailable: Metal prices could not be loaded right now, so no value is shown. Check again a little later.
Calculator.noPrices: Today's CBAR price has not arrived yet, so no value is shown.
Calculator.howText: Metal value = weight in grams × fineness ÷ 1000 × CBAR price of 1 gram of pure metal. CBAR publishes metal rates in manat per troy ounce (31.1034768 g); we convert them to grams and round the result to the nearest qəpik.

price.q: Why is a shop price higher than the metal value?
price.a: A shop price also includes workmanship, stones, the store's margin and other costs. The calculator shows only the value of the metal in the piece.

fineness.a: Fineness is the share of pure metal in parts per thousand: 585 gold is 58.5% pure gold, 925 silver is 92.5% pure silver.

source.q: Where do the prices come from?
source.a: From the daily precious metal rates of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan (CBAR). On weekends and holidays the last published rate is used.

method.source: Every business day the Central Bank of Azerbaijan (CBAR) publishes rates for bank metals (gold, silver, platinum, palladium) in manat per troy ounce of pure metal.
method.gram: The ounce price is divided by 31.1034768 (the grams in a troy ounce) to get the price of 1 gram of pure metal.
method.fineness: The pure gram price is multiplied by the fineness: 585 gold is 58.5% gold, so its gram price is 0.585 of the pure price. The result is rounded to 0.01 manat.
method.weekend: On weekends and holidays CBAR publishes no new rate, so the last published rate stays in force; the date above is the date of that rate.
method.jewelry: These are metal values, not jewelry prices. A piece also includes labor, stones and the store's margin, and the store confirms the final price.

Verified.title: How we verify
Verified.description: What the Jeparla Verified badge means and what it does not: seller, document and physical expertise checks, the complaint process and the seller code of conduct.
Verified.lead: "Jeparla Verified" is not one check but three. Each is shown separately on product and store pages. Here we say plainly what each check covers and what it does not.
Verified.badgeRule: The badge appears only when both the seller check and the document check have passed.

seller.title: Seller
seller.what: That the store is real: name, address, contact number and tax ID (VÖEN) or sole trader registration.
seller.not: It does not check service quality or individual sales.

documents.title: Documents
documents.what: Documents the seller uploads: registration certificate, VÖEN certificate or hallmark stamp document. Documents are stored privately and never shown publicly.
documents.who: The Jeparla team, by hand; every decision is logged.
documents.not: It does not confirm the fineness and weight of each product separately.

expertise.title: Physical expertise
expertise.what: An expert looks at the product itself: fineness, weight and stones.
expertise.who: An independent expert or laboratory. Expertise was done only where the product shows "Verified".
expertise.not: We do not claim a product marked "Not performed" was physically checked.

Verified.limits: No check is a full guarantee. Before buying, check the hallmark, the weight and the receipt in the store. The sale and payment are between the store and the buyer.

complaint.1: On the product page you choose a reason under "Report" and add a note. No account needed.
complaint.2: The complaint goes to the admin queue; the team checks the product, the store and the documents again.
complaint.3: If needed, the product is hidden or returned to the seller for correction. For serious or repeated violations the store can be suspended.

Verified.responseTime: We do not give a response time yet: we will only publish one we can actually keep.
Verified.codeIntro: This is what we expect from stores selling on Jeparla. Violations are checked through complaints.

code.1: Fineness and weight are stated correctly and match the product's hallmark.
code.2: No unhallmarked precious metal items are sold.
code.3: If the product and terms have not changed, the buyer is not quoted a higher price than shown on Jeparla.
code.4: Stones are described honestly: natural, lab-grown or imitation; certificate numbers are given correctly.
code.5: Photos show the actual product; AI-generated images are labelled.
code.6: No fake reviews, fake discounts or invented numbers.
code.7: The buyer's contact details are used only to answer them and for the sale.
code.8: The buyer's consumer rights (an accurate description, a receipt, the warranty, replacement of a faulty item or a refund) are respected as the law requires; no condition limits them.

meaning.q: What does the Jeparla Verified badge mean?
meaning.a: It shows that the store passed the seller check and the document check. Physical expertise is a separate status shown on each product.

guarantee.a: No. Checks lower the risk but are not a full guarantee. Before buying, check the hallmark and weight and ask for a receipt.

report.q: What should I do if a product looks suspicious?
report.a: Press "Report" on the product page. The team checks the product and the store again.

Verified.codeAcceptance: Sellers accept the code when they apply and confirm it again once a year in the cabinet. Without it no product can be sent to review. The acceptance date is shown on the store page.

PricesMonthly.title: Gold and silver prices in Azerbaijan: monthly overview
PricesMonthly.description: The price of 1 gram of gold and silver each month from the daily rates of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan: first and last day, lowest, highest, average and change, in manat.
PricesMonthly.lead: For each month, the price of 1 gram of gold and silver is computed from the CBAR rates Jeparla stores every business day. No number is typed in, and none is a forecast.
PricesMonthly.error: The price history could not be loaded right now. Please look again a little later.
PricesMonthly.summary: 1 gram of 585 gold cost {first} on the first rate day of the month (<d1>{firstDay}</d1>) and {last} on the last (<d2>{lastDay}</d2>), a change of {change}. The lowest price in the month was {low}, the highest {high} ({quotes, plural, one {# rate day} other {# rate days}}).
PricesMonthly.caption: Price of 1 gram, in manat. Metal value only.
PricesMonthly.quotes: {count, plural, one {# rate day.} other {# rate days.}}

method.source: Source: the bank metal rates CBAR publishes every business day (1 troy ounce of pure metal, in manat). Jeparla stores them daily; the overview is built only from stored days.
method.stats: The price of 1 gram is the ounce price divided by 31.1034768, multiplied by the fineness for an alloy, and rounded to the qəpik. "Average" is the plain mean of the rate days in the month, "change" runs from the first to the last day.
method.gaps: CBAR publishes no rate on weekends and holidays; those days are not part of the figures. While the current month is running, the last day is the last stored rate day.
method.corrected: An asterisk (*) means a Jeparla admin corrected a CBAR rate in that month.
method.jewelry: These are metal values, not jewellery prices: the price of a piece also includes the work, the stones and the store's margin.
